metadata.title: The Primes Contain Arbitrarily Long Arithmetic Progressions (Green & Tao, 2004)
metadata.framework: Transference principle transferring Szemeredi's theorem from dense subsets of integers to the primes via a pseudorandom majorant
metadata.source_note: Extraction based on arXiv:math/0404188 PDF text.

nodes.name: Arithmetic progression in the primes
nodes.statement: An arithmetic progression of length $k$ in the primes is a sequence $p, p+d, p+2d, \ldots, p+(k-1)d$ where all terms are prime. The main theorem states these exist for every $k$.

nodes.name: Pseudorandom measure
nodes.statement:
A measure $
u: \mathbb{Z}_N 	o \mathbb{R}^+$ with $\mathbb{E}[
u] = 1 + o(1)$ is $(k, \epsilon)$-pseudorandom if it satisfies a linear forms condition and a correlation condition. The linear forms condition requires that for any system of at most $k$ linear forms in at most $k$ unknowns, the average of $
u$ over solutions is close to 1.

nodes.name: W-trick and modified von Mangoldt function
nodes.statement: Define $W = \prod_{p \leq w} p$ for a slowly growing $w$. The modified von Mangoldt function $\tilde{\Lambda}(n) = \frac{\phi(W)}{W} \Lambda(Wn + b)$ for appropriate residue class $b$ removes small-prime biases, making the resulting measure approximately pseudorandom on $[N/W]$.

nodes.name: Green-Tao theorem (main result)
nodes.statement: The prime numbers contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions. Equivalently, for every $k \geq 1$, there exist primes $p_1 < p_2 < \cdots < p_k$ forming an arithmetic progression.

nodes.name: Relative Szemeredi theorem (transference principle)
nodes.statement: Let $\nu$ be a $k$-pseudorandom measure on $\mathbb{Z}_N$ and let $f: \mathbb{Z}_N \to \mathbb{R}^+$ satisfy $0 \leq f(n) \leq \nu(n)$ for all $n$ and $\mathbb{E}[f] \geq \delta > 0$. Then $f$ contains the expected number of $k$-term arithmetic progressions, up to a small error: $\mathbb{E}_{n,d} f(n)f(n+d) \cdots f(n+(k-1)d) \geq c(k, \delta) - o(1)$.

nodes.name: Szemeredi's theorem (used as black box)
nodes.statement: Any subset $A \subseteq \{1, \ldots, N\}$ of positive upper density ($|A|/N \geq \delta > 0$) contains arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions. This is the classical result of Szemeredi (1975) that serves as one of the three main ingredients.

nodes.name: Goldston-Yildirim estimate
nodes.statement: There exists a function $\nu$ majorizing (a suitable modification of) the von Mangoldt function $\Lambda$ such that $\nu$ is pseudorandom in the required sense. This uses results from the Goldston-Yildirim sieve, showing that a suitable truncated divisor sum $\Lambda_R$ provides the required pseudorandom majorant with $\Lambda_R(n) \geq \Lambda(n)/\log R$ on a dense set.

nodes.name: Proof structure of Green-Tao
nodes.statement: Three ingredients: (1) Szemeredi's theorem for dense sets. (2) A transference principle: any subset of a pseudorandom set with positive relative density inherits the arithmetic progression property. (3) Construction of a pseudorandom majorant for the primes using the Goldston-Yildirim sieve. Combining: the primes have positive relative density in the pseudorandom majorant, so by transference + Szemeredi, they contain long APs.

nodes.name: Primes have density zero but positive relative density
nodes.statement: By the prime number theorem, the primes have density zero in $\{1, \ldots, N\}$ ($\pi(N) \sim N/\log N$), so Szemeredi's theorem cannot be applied directly. The key insight is to embed the primes in a pseudorandom set where they have positive relative density, then transfer Szemeredi's theorem to this setting.

nodes.name: Quantitative bounds
nodes.statement: The proof is effective but gives extremely weak quantitative bounds (tower-type in $k$), inherited from the use of Szemeredi's theorem. Using the Gowers-norm-based proof of Szemeredi's theorem gives better (but still very large) bounds.
